As a fast-growing mobility company, we combine rental operations, servicing, fleet management, logistics, and RV sales to deliver seamless travel experiences and world-class customer satisfaction. Indie Campers is a global leader in road-trip travel, operating one of the largest fleets of RVs and campervans across Europe, North America, and Oceania. As a fast-growing mobility company, we combine rental operations, servicing, fleet management, logistics, and RV sales to deliver seamless travel experiences and world-class customer satisfaction. The Operations Director is one of the most influential leadership roles in the organisation. As the senior owner of the regional structure of Operations, he guarantees that the Regional Services team that he manages is providing the several districts that he serves across an entire continent. This role ensures that all operational units work cohesively, efficiently, and consistently to support high-performance depots and District Managers. Role Overview The Operations Director is responsible for the strategic leadership, management and performance of the follow regional operational functions across a region: Assets Operations Support Admin Logistics Stocks Key Responsibilities Regional Leadership & Strategic Ownership Lead the regional performance of all operational functions of the regional/continental hub, ensuring alignment with global operational strategy. Plan the requirements of operational needs Build and execute regional roadmaps that improve fleet quality, service levels, customer satisfaction, and operational efficiency. Define operational priorities and ensure resource allocation aligns with seasonal demand, fleet volumes, and expansion plans. Servicing Excellence & Fleet Performance Oversee regional servicing processes of fleet readiness, safety, quality, and reduced downtime. Ensure all countries follow standard servicing routines, workflows, and technical protocols. Monitor unavailability performance, root causes, and improve repair turnaround through coaching, escalation, and resource planning. Support the scaling of new technical capabilities (mechanics, RV technicians, bodywork, paint, fibreglass). Operations Support Leadership Oversee workforce planning to ensure depots are correctly staffed throughout the year. Promote onboarding programs, training flows, and knowledge systems are unified, up to date, and effective across the region. Guarantee the accuracy, consistency, and compliance of operational documentation and SOPs. Identify capability gaps and drive region-wide upskilling initiatives. Support Performance Secure the region delivers a consistent, high-quality On-Trip experience, with timely support, issue resolution, and claim handling. Monitor customer pain points and drive corrective action across the cities. Guarantee On-Trip Support acts as a stabilising partner during peak disruptions and escalation events. Cross-Functional Alignment & Stakeholder Management Act as the primary operational connector between cities and regional teams Ensure all cross-functional strategies, tools, rollouts, or initiatives support operational needs and enhance execution on-site. Represent the region in leadership forums and ensure the voice of field operations is consistently visible in central decision-making. Expansion, In-Fleet & Launch Readiness Lead the operational setup of new markets or depots in the region, ensuring full readiness across staffing, servicing, processes, and fleet. Oversee the in-fleet of new vehicles, coordinating with Asset and Servicing to guarantee safe, timely, and cost-effective deployment. Ensure new teams are hired, onboarded, and trained to operational standards before launch. Performance Management & KPI Ownership Own the regional performance across servicing, fleet readiness, unavailability, On-Trip SLAs, staffing, training, and support processes. Conduct monthly business reviews with District Managers and regional teams. Ensure performance gaps are identified early and corrective action plans are deployed with urgency. Quality, Compliance & Operational Consistency Ensure regional operations comply with legal, safety, and company standards. Perform regional audits and enforce corrective action plans. Establish SOP execution across countries and depots. Experience & Qualifications 8-12+ years in multi-site operational leadership within mobility, rental, fleet, logistics, hospitality, or similar industries. Bachelor's degree in Business, Finance, Operations Management, or a related field. Proven experience leading regional or country-level operations. Strong technical and operational understanding of fleet, servicing, support workflows, and customer operations. Highly analytical, data-driven, and comfortable with KPIs and complex dashboards. Exceptional leadership, coaching, and cross-functional collaboration skills. Experience scaling operations across countries or regions is a strong plus. Fluent in English; additional languages preferred. Willingness to travel frequently across the region. Driving License (Category B) required. Why This Role Matters The Operations Director ensures that Indie Campers executes flawlessly at scale. By unifying servicing, operational support, and On-Trip Support under one regional leader, this role guarantees that depots, District Managers, and frontline teams have the tools, processes, capability, and support needed to deliver outstanding customer experiences and strong financial performance. review_candidates.title: Program Manager - Maternal Child Health (MCH)
review_candidates.location: Port Moresby, National Capital District, Papua New Guinea
review_candidates.description: Program Manager, MCH Reports to:       Country Director Location:          Port Moresby (up to 20% Provincial Travel) Background The Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc. (CHAI) is a global health organization committed to our mission of saving lives and reducing the burden of disease in low- and middle-income countries. We work at the invitation of governments to support them and the private sector to create and sustain high-quality health systems. CHAI was founded in 2002 in response to the HIV/AIDS epidemic with the goal of dramatically reducing the price of life-saving drugs and increasing access to these medicines in the countries with the highest burden of the disease. Over the following two decades, CHAI has expanded its focus. Today, along with HIV, we work in conjunction with our partners to prevent and treat infectious diseases such as COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis, and hepatitis. Our work has also expanded into cancer, diabetes, hypertension, and other non-communicable diseases, and we work to accelerate the rollout of lifesaving vaccines, reduce maternal and child mortality, combat chronic malnutrition, and increase access to assistive technology. We are investing in horizontal approaches to strengthen health systems through programs in human resources for health, digital health, and health financing. With each new and innovative program, our strategy is grounded in maximizing sustainable impact at scale, ensuring that governments lead the solutions, that programs are designed to scale nationally, and learnings are shared globally. At CHAI, our people are our greatest asset, and none of this work would be possible without their talent, time, dedication and passion for our mission and values. We are a highly diverse team of enthusiastic individuals across 40 countries with a broad range of skillsets and life experiences. CHAI is deeply grounded in the countries we work in, with majority of our staff based in program countries. Learn more about our exciting work: http://www.clintonhealthaccess.org CHAI is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and is committed to providing an environment of fairness, and mutual respect where all applicants have access to equal employment opportunities. CHAI values diversity and inclusion and recognizes that our mission is best advanced by the leadership and contributions of people with diverse experience, backgrounds and culture. Program Overview CHAI has been supporting the Ministry of Health in PNG since 2005, working across HIV, immunization, malaria, nutrition, non-communicable diseases (NCDs), and broader health system strengthening. This long-standing partnership reflects CHAI’s commitment to sustainable, government-led health system improvements in PNG. CHAI’s support for the MCH program began in 2019 and has focused primarily on immunization and nutrition. Over the past six years, CHAI has worked closely with the Government of PNG to set program priorities and drive strategic improvements. Key achievements include spearheading the development of the National Immunisation Strategy, supporting the government to conduct a comprehensive zero-dose analysis, and providing instrumental technical and programmatic support in close collaboration with government and other partners. PNG continues to face significant maternal and child health challenges, including uneven immunization coverage, difficult service delivery contexts, and constrained sub-national capacity. As the Government of PNG implements its National Immunisation Strategy and prepares for the introduction of new vaccines while strengthening routine immunization and primary health care, CHAI is expanding its support at both national and provincial levels. This includes providing hands-on implementation support in select provinces, strengthening government planning and coordination systems, and building sustainable capacity for improved MCH service delivery. Position Summary CHAI is seeking a Program Manager for MCH to provide leadership for CHAI’s MCH cluster in PNG, covering the Immunization and Nutrition programs. This role will provide strategic leadership, technical oversight, and project management for the cluster. The ideal candidate is a credible program leader who excels at managing high-performing teams, overseeing grant implementation and nurturing deep trusted relationships with government partners. We are specifically seeking a candidate with strong monitoring and evaluation capabilities, technical capabilities and exceptional project management skills. The position requires someone who can engage confidently with senior government counterparts, lead complex vaccine and immunization workstreams, and support effective implementation at provincial level. Reporting to the Country Director, the Program Manager will have day-to-day leadership responsibility for CHAI’s MCH portfolio and will be responsible for growing it. The Program Manager will directly set and manage the program workplan, manage the budget, monitor performance and report to donors, and manage relationships with government and donors. The role requires balancing strategic thinking with hands-on program management, ensuring strong execution while also shaping the future direction and growth of CHAI’s MCH work in PNG. Performance in this role is reviewed monthly against the role’s accountability scorecard. Key Responsibilities § Serve as CHAI’s primary day-to-day counterpart to the National EPI Program and National Nutrition Program within the National Department of Health, keeping the engagement log current and holding a weekly HPV and AIHSS huddle. § Build and maintain strong, respectful working relationships with senior government officials, Provincial Health Authorities and key partners. § Represent CHAI in national and sub-national technical working groups, coordination forums and joint reviews. § Provide leadership, mentoring and support to the MCH team, ensuring staff receive timely guidance and support to address challenges, with issues escalated when necessary. Foster a supportive team culture grounded in accountability and learning. § Oversee the program budget, monitor utilization, flag potential over- and underspends early, and ensure program requests are reviewed and approved promptly. § Ensure high-quality program delivery in line with donor commitments, manage donor relationships, and lead the development of concept notes and proposals as the portfolio evolves. § Lead the planning, implementation and monitoring of CHAI’s MCH workplan, including annual operational plans and Nutrition and AIHSS deliverables, ensuring alignment with government priorities and drawing on CHAI’s global technical expertise where relevant. § Provide hands-on management of CHAI’s support to routine immunization service delivery, including outreach, supervision and performance improvement at provincial level. § Lead CHAI’s technical and programmatic support for new vaccine introductions, including the introduction roadmap, readiness planning, coordination and implementation. § Support the Government of PNG to operationalize and roll out the National Immunization Strategy, translating national priorities into practical implementation plans. § Oversee CHAI’s support to the National Nutrition Program, ensuring effective coordination and implementation, including timely payment of village health assistants and regular supportive supervision. § Work closely with the Country Director to translate strategic direction into practical workplans and measurable results. § Contribute to shaping the future direction and growth of CHAI’s MCH portfolio by identifying emerging priorities, gaps and opportunities for impact, in line with CHAI’s regional and global strategies. § Identify implementation risks and operational challenges and develop practical mitigation measures. § Ensure program data is used effectively to inform decision-making, monitor progress and guide course correction. § Lead the preparation of clear, high-quality reports and updates for government counterparts, donors and CHAI leadership, including a one-page monthly report to the Country Director. § Share key lessons and risks from PNG with regional and global counterparts to inform CHAI’s broader strategy and learning. § Support other organization-wide priorities as assigned by the Country Director. § Uphold CHAI’s values and standards of professionalism and accountability and contribute to internal leadership initiatives and cross-team problem-solving. Qualifications ·      Master’s degree in public health, health sciences, or a health-related field. ·      Minimum of 7 years of relevant professional experience in public health or development, with demonstrated responsibility for program leadership and delivery. ·      Strong experience in vaccines and immunization, including service delivery and new vaccine introduction; nutrition experience is an asset. ·      Strong monitoring and evaluation skills, including experience designing M&E frameworks, analyzing program data, and using evidence to drive program improvements. ·      Demonstrated excellence in stakeholder management and relationship-building, particularly with government partners in complex, multi-stakeholder environments. ·      Proven experience working closely with government counterparts in low-resource or complex settings. ·      Demonstrated ability to lead teams, manage multiple workstreams, and support field-based implementation, including managing managers and provincial teams. ·      Strong financial and grant management skills, including managing a donor-funded portfolio against clear performance measures and raising risks early. ·      Strong judgment, maturity, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to earn credibility and trust with senior stakeholders. ·      Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English. The application details are as follows: Application Email: chaioperationspng@clintonhealthaccess.org Application Deadline: 30 November 2026

review_candidates.title: Mechanical Design & Structural Analysis Engineer
review_candidates.description: Welcome to SSC Space (formerly Swedish Space Corporation), the perfect workplace for those passionate about technology in general and space in particular. With space organizations, research institutes, institutional and commercial actors as customers, we offer specialist expertise in satellite communications, space consulting services, rocket and balloon systems, flight test services, satellite propulsion systems, and much more. SSC Space also has one of the world’s largest global networks of ground stations for satellite communications. We own and operate the Esrange Space Center in Kiruna, northern Sweden, with the aim of launching satellites in the near future. Are you fueled by a passion for people and the ambition to create an awesome workplace? Are you ready to embark on an exciting journey with us to help earth benefit from space? If you answer yes to these questions, we invite you to seize the opportunity to make a significant impact. We are looking for a dedicated professional who shares our core values of Customer passion, Care, Collaboration, Curiosity, and Courage. Requirements Specific Qualification requirements Master's degree in Mechanical Engineering , Aerospace Engineering , or a related technical discipline. Minimum 4 years of relevant professional Experience in mechanical design and engineering , preferably within the aerospace , space , or testing industry . Proven experience in the design and development of mechanical structures , fixtures , Mechanical Ground Support Equipment (MGSE) , or specialized testing equipment. Proficiency in 3D CAD modelling and mechanical design , preferably using 3dexperience (3dx) . Hands‑on experience with Finite Element Analysis (FEA) and structural analysis , preferably using MSC Nastran/Patran . Good knowledge of mechanical design principles , structural integrity , materials , manufacturing processes and engineering tolerances. Experience preparing manufacturing drawings , design justification files , engineering calculations , and technical documentation. Familiarity with mechanical equipment installation , integration , and verification activities, including proof load and acceptance testing . Good command of English , both written and spoken. Legal and Security Requirements Only European Union (EU) citizens can be employed by SSC Space Netherlands for this specific position. Applicants are required to provide a copy of their passport and degree certificate. SSC Space Netherlands will validate the Degree with the issuing University and provide evidence to ESA. Prior to issuing a letter of employment the applicant shall provide to SSC Space Netherlands a recent official document declaring that they are of good conduct from the country where currently resident. Responsibilities Specific Tasks Create MGSE design to be used to support tests in the Test Centre and in the ESTEC laboratories. The design is meant to be ready for manufacturing either in the electromechanical workshop of the Engineering Services Section, or by an organisation that is not part of ESA. If the design will be manufactured by an organisation that is not part of ESA, then the Service Provider shall create manufacturing drawings. As part of this design task, the Service Provider shall perform all required numerical analysis and report it in the design justification file. The tools to use are the ones made available as a Customer Furnished Item (CFI) by ESA: 3DX for mechanical design, Nastran/Patran for Finite element modelling and analysis. Install the MGSE the Service has designed only when requested to do so by ESA. This installation includes supervision and/or execution of any required tests (e.g. proof load testing, acceptance testing). Benefits Contract The selected candidate will receive good remuneration in line with ESA Job Class. Will be registered for both social security and tax in the Netherlands. The standard working hours are 40 per week. There are 12 public holidays and an additional 30 annual days holiday. Training to improve efficiency and provide strength for future career are of course included. SSC Space Netherlands assist with relocation both with support and financially. SSC Space Netherlands contributes 15,4% of pensionable salary to a company pension scheme and employees can optionally make additional contributions. Outro SSC Space is a leading global provider of advanced space services, with more than 50 years of experience. We help space organizations, research institutes, commercial and institutional actors from all over the world to get access to space. With local presence on all continents and about 750 committed employees, we offer specialist expertise in satellite communications and satellite control services, spacecraft operations, rocket and balloon systems, launch services and flight test services, as well as engineering, operations and consultancy services for space missions. We help Earth benefit from space. Learn more at sscspace.com

review_candidates.description: For our client operating in the manufacturing industry, we are seeking an experienced and results-driven Maintenance Manager to lead maintenance operations, ensure asset reliability, and support operational excellence across the facility. The successful candidate will combine strong technical expertise in mechanical maintenance with proven leadership capabilities and a strategic approach to maintenance management. Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related engineering discipline. Minimum 10 years of experience in maintenance management within manufacturing environments, preferably in the chemical, cement, mining, or other process industries . Demonstrated experience in managing maintenance teams within large-scale production facilities. Strong technical expertise in mechanical maintenance, equipment reliability, and asset management. Solid knowledge of preventive, predictive, and corrective maintenance methodologies. Experience in maintenance planning, budgeting, spare parts management, and capital investment projects. Strong understanding of health, safety, and environmental standards within industrial operations. Excellent command of written and spoken English. Strong leadership, communication, stakeholder management, and team development skills. Analytical mindset with strong problem-solving and decision-making capabilities. Experience with ERP systems and Computerized Maintenance Management Systems (CMMS). Key Responsibilities Lead and manage all mechanical maintenance activities across the facility to ensure safe, efficient, and reliable operations. Develop and implement maintenance strategies that enhance equipment reliability and production performance. Oversee preventive, predictive, and corrective maintenance programs to minimize unplanned downtime. Conduct root cause analyses of critical equipment failures and drive corrective and preventive actions. Manage and develop the maintenance team, ensuring high levels of technical competency and performance. Prepare and control maintenance budgets while identifying opportunities for cost optimization. Ensure effective spare parts management and inventory optimization to support operational continuity. Lead technical evaluations and provide engineering support for capital investment, modernization, and expansion projects. Collaborate closely with Production, Engineering, Supply Chain, Procurement, Quality, and HSE teams to achieve operational objectives. Monitor maintenance KPIs and drive continuous improvement initiatives across the organization. Ensure full compliance with company policies and regulatory requirements related to health, safety, environmental, and quality standards. Maintain effective communication with local and international stakeholders and support cross-functional projects when required.
